body.x: 'CES 2014(The International Consumer Electronics Show)' will be soon opened. As the show gets last minutes, CES proposes 10 things which you do not want to miss at the show floor. Check the details on events, exciting exhibits and other useful information. 'The 2014 International CES' is the biggest IT∙appliances show held in Las Vegas, U.S. from January 7th to 10th.
1. Press Day Shuttles (complimentary from LVCC and official CES hotels)
An easy way to get to Mandalay Bay for the press events.
2. Startup Technology

The Eureka Park TechZone will feature more than 200 entrepreneurs and startups, plus the new Eureka Park: NEXT TechZone, a dedicated area designed for mid-stage startups that have launched a product within the past year. Academia Tech is within Eureka Park and focuses on the unique technologies coming from colleges and universities.
3. Driverless Car Experience
Sponsored by Bosch, this all-new TechZone will feature a variety of technologies that support the future of autonomous/automated driving
including parking assist, collision avoidance
4. 3D Printing TechZone
Sponsored by TCT Mag + Personalize, this new area will showcase the latest in 3D printing making it more accessible for today’s consumers.
Home to industry leaders Makerbot, 3D Systems and Stratasys, the future of printing come to life on the show floor of CES. (LVCC, South Hall 3)
5. MotionTech TechZone

Sponsored by MEMS Industry Group, MotionTech is an all-new TechZone, showcasing leading innovation in sensor technology, including MEMS, the smallest motion-sensing devices. From gesture recognition and augmented reality, to eye-tracking technology and motion sensors, attendees will discover new ways to connect and interact with their devices. (LVCC, South Hall 2)
6. Tech Titans and Technology

Innovators Keynotes are set. The Tech Titans Keynotes are leaders from the most powerful companies in technology including Brian Krzanich, Intel Kazou Hirai, Sony Rupert Stadler, Audi AG Marissa Mayer, Yahoo! Gary Shapiro, CEA John Chambers, and more.

Plus, The Technology Innovators Keynotes offer insights from innovators, thought leaders and disruptors – the “rock stars” of their industries ; John Donovan, AT&T Andrew England, MillerCoors Hans Vestberg, Ericsson Carolyn Everson, Facebook Dr. Paul E. Jacobs, Qualcomm James D. Farley, Jr., Ford Motor Co. Dick Costolo, Twitter Maurice Levy, Publicis Groupe Scott Dorsey, Marketing Cloud
7. Gary’s Book Club

Presented by Barnes & Noble, Gary’s Book Club showcases the works of prominent authors in the tech industry. Attendees have the opportunity to meet the authors, purchase books and have copies signed. Book signings will follow lively discussions by the authors on the Experience CEA stage. (LVCC, Grand Lobby)
8. Cisco’s Internet of Everything

The Internet of Everything (IoE) brings together people, process, data, and things to make networked connections. the Cisco Internet of Everything TechZone offers experience IoE in action and the unprecedented opportunities it creates. (LVCC, Central Hall)
9. Breakthrough of the Year Awards
Variety’s 2014 Breakthrough of the Year Awards celebrate a diverse range of extraordinary talent in the fields of film, television, sport, music, comedy, technology, philanthropy and social media.
10. Wearable Technology
From jackets that adjust based on outside temperature to solar-charging handbags and health monitoring devices, the industry. (The Venetian, Level 2, Venetian Ballroom)

'CES 2014(The International Consumer Electronics Show)' is owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), the technology trade association. CES showcases more than 3,200 exhibitors, including manufacturers, developers and suppliers of consumer technology hardware, content, technology delivery systems and more; a conference and more than 152,000 attendees from more than 150 countries. The first CES took place in New York City in June of 1967. Since then, thousands of products have been announced at the yearly show in January.
